about: Playtest scenarios for `bash scripts/game/playtest.sh`. Each is `ak create` run with these arguments, so the Allocator prices every level and the personas build it as they would for a player. {A} is the player's affinity and {B} its opposite; {C} and {D} are another opposed pair; {T1} and {T2} are two kinds whose affinity-table row carries a trait (soak, spread, raise), so every trait comes up across seeds. The seed picks the affinities, so every affinity comes up across runs. tests/simulations/playtest-scenarios.test.mjs builds and runs each one with every affinity as the player's; `knownIssues` lists rule breaks still open, as tests/simulations/scenarios do. A scenario with --tactic is built with --seed set to its seed, so the tactic's placement replays too. `shows` is the one-line summary the scenario list prints.

scenarios.title: First look
scenarios.shows: fog and sight, the HUD (hits and regen per vital), sprint, loot, the exit/defeat line
focus: Walk both rooms and find the exit: does fog and sight feel right?
Read the HUD: each vital shows what hit it and what regen gave back, e.g. HP 18/20 (−2 +1). Does it match what happened?
Sprint: shift + a move (or x, then a move) goes two tiles for 3× the stamina. Worth it?
Take the resource (g): it stays intact, and the vital it raises goes up.
Get near the warden: does it notice you, and what does its push do? The in-sight line says what you can see of it.
Reach the exit (or fall): the event line should say who left or was defeated.

scenarios.title: Walking through fields
scenarios.shows: hazard fields, a minefield room with a safe line, drained sources going dim and off
focus: One room is a minefield: overlapping hazard fields with a safe line along its edge, and a reward inside. Find the line.
Stand in each hazard's field: does the HUD change the way the colour suggests?
Walk your own {A} field into the {B} hazard: do they cancel on the cells between?
Watch durability and health: which vital takes the hit first?
Leave your emit on until mana drains: does it switch off, and back on when full? A drained hazard dims, drops its field and shows as off.

scenarios.title: Duel with a warden
scenarios.shows: free aim, cast arrows and hit lines, push and pull, raising barriers (z), range and intensity
focus: Cast push and pull at the warden (f, Tab, Enter): the path shows as arrows for a turn and the hit is named. Does it match the panel?
Aim at an empty tile (f, then move keys, Enter): the cast travels the line; a push that meets nobody leaves a one-turn field.
A pull draws only its own row's vital from the warden: check which one moves.
Raise a barrier line between you (z, aim, Enter), then fight round it.
Change range and intensity in the list (i, then + - ] [): does the mana cost follow?
Run out of mana mid-fight, then win or lose: is the end of the fight clear on screen?

scenarios.title: Affinity traits
scenarios.shows: two trait kinds in your hands: soak slows, spread creeps (raise has no effect yet)
focus: You carry {T1} and {T2} pushes (the start line names their traits). Hit the wardens with each and watch what the trait adds.
soak: a soaked actor pays more stamina per move for a few turns.
spread: where the push lands a field creeps on, a tile a turn, weaker each step. raise has no effect of its own yet (any kind can raise barriers with z).
The wardens fight back with {B} and {D}: does anything stack up unfairly?

scenarios.title: Party and orders
scenarios.shows: switching delvers, companion orders, companions taking loot
focus: Switch between your two delvers (Tab): does the view and HUD follow?
Order the companion (o): follow, guard, then change its order mid-game.
Does the companion help, get in the way, or get stuck? Does it take the resource, leaving it intact?
Get everyone to the exit: the event line should say who has left.

scenarios.title: Ambush and retinue
scenarios.shows: a loot room with guards hidden out of doorway sight, and a boss warden with minions
focus: One room holds loot with two guards hidden out of sight of its doorways: they hold until they see you, then strike. Can you spot the trap?
A boss warden leads a retinue: a shield emitting its kind, a support restoring it, a striker. Who do you take out first?
Is the loot worth the fight, and can you sneak round it?

scenarios.title: Long haul
scenarios.shows: a long level whose tactics the Director picks from the seed (--tactic auto), at your chosen grade
focus: Play to the exit or to defeat: is the pacing fun, or does it drag?
Rest when stamina runs low: is recovery worth the turns?
Do the wardens defend sensibly, or loop or stall?
Note anything priced oddly: too strong, too weak, too cheap.
The Director picked this level's tactics from the seed (the start line names them): did they make it more interesting?
Try a grade: --grade H (easiest) to S. Does the difficulty step feel right?

scenarios.title: Hits pause regen
scenarios.shows: a push or pull hit stops regen for 3 turns (#478); pull costs the same mana as push (#532)
focus: Open the panel (i): your {A} push and pull at the same range and intensity now show the same mana cost (#532).
Hit the warden with a push (f, Tab, Enter). Its HUD vitals should show regen 0 on the vital that was hit, plus health, durability and stamina, for that turn and the next 3. Mana keeps regenerating.
Hit it again before the 3 turns end: the pause restarts from that hit.
Keep hitting every few turns: its health should now fall to defeat instead of regenerating back (it used to stalemate).
Stand in a field instead of casting: fields do not pause regen (only cast hits do).
The warden hits you too: the same pause shows on your HUD.

scenarios.title: Draw reach
scenarios.shows: a draw of range r reaches r+1 tiles and eases off in a line (#533)
focus: You emit a {A} draw at range 3 (start line, panel i). Stand a warden-free distance away and walk toward the hazard-free board edge: the draw field should cover 4 tiles from you, weaker toward the edge (colour dims).
Walk the warden's {B} hazard emit into your field: cells nearer you should steal more than the far ones.
Draw used to reach one tile only, at full strength: a field one tile out should now be weaker than at your own tile, and tiles 2-4 out should still show.
Draw still steals and absorbs; check the warden's vital moves while it stands inside your reach.

scenarios.title: Earth builds, corrode breaks
scenarios.shows: earth raises barriers with twice the durability (#534); corrode does double harm to structures (#535)
focus: Raise a barrier with earth (equip earth:push in the panel i, then z, aim, Enter). Note its durability in inspect/panel; compare with a barrier raised by another kind (the warden's {B} push, or any non-earth slot): earth's is about twice as strong for twice the mana.
Switch to corrode:push (i) and hit your earth barrier, then the hazard and the resource: each takes about twice the damage a non-corrode push of the same range and intensity does.
Corrode hitting the warden is normal strength (its defeat vital is health): the double applies to barriers, hazards and resources only.
Same-kind immunity still holds: a corrode barrier is not breached by corrode.

scenarios.title: Wind knockback
scenarios.shows: wind knocks back twice as far as other kinds (#536)
focus: Push the warden with wind at intensity 2 (f, Tab, Enter): it should fly 4 cells (intensity x2 steps), stopping early at a wall or actor.
Switch to the {B} push at the same intensity (i, then equip): it moves 2 cells. Every kind still knocks back, wind just goes further.
A pull from wind drags the target toward you by the same extra distance.
Push it into a wall: it stops there. Push so it lands in a hazard field if you can.

scenarios.title: Restoring steals top up
scenarios.shows: a restoring kind (growth, fortify, light) steals only what it lacks (#537)
focus: You carry growth pulls. At full health, pull the warden (f, Tab, Enter): you gain nothing and its health is untouched (a full caster takes nothing).
Let the warden hurt you (it pushes decay/{B}), then pull again: you take only as much health as you lack, never past your max.
Check the warden: it loses exactly what you gained, not the full pull amount.
A harmful kind's steal (the warden's pull, if it has one) still takes the whole amount regardless of room.

scenarios.title: Line of fire
scenarios.shows: a warden's cast at you follows the tile line: walls and allies in between stop or take it (#538)
focus: Two wardens hunt you. Stand with a wall corner between you and one of them: its cast stops at the wall instead of reaching you (it used to ignore walls).
Line the wardens up so one stands between you and the other: the front one takes the back one's cast (friendly fire), and the price is paid either way.
Raise a barrier (z) across the line: casts at you should hit it.
Casts at yourself (own emit) still work as before.

scenarios.title: Shrines and healing wells
scenarios.shows: restoring hazards off the route (#486); --tactic auto can pick them too (#531)
focus: The level has shrine hazards in a room off the spawn-to-exit route (the start line names them; a health one is a healing well). Find one.
Stand in its field: the HUD should show the vital it restores climbing each turn. Is it worth the detour?
Hurt yourself on the warden first, then visit it.
Run again with other --seed values: the shrine kinds are drawn from the restoring rows (growth, fortify, light) by the seed.
For the auto mix run `long-haul` on several seeds: shrines can now appear among its tactics (#531).

scenarios.title: Full budget: big level
scenarios.shows: six large rooms, wardens and traps built from the whole budget (95% spent)
focus: The start line gives the spend: about 95% of the budget goes on the rooms, the traps and the wardens, and your delver's share on you. ak create splits a budget into shares (rooms, traps, wardens, your delver); this level is sized so every share is nearly spent.
Four wardens guard six large rooms and two strong traps: does the level feel full, or empty between fights?
Your delver is built from its whole share, so it is strong: is it too strong for what the dungeon could buy?

scenarios.title: Full budget: vast level
scenarios.shows: ten large rooms, six wardens and four traps from the whole budget (97% spent)
focus: Ten large rooms on a 56 by 56 board, with the whole budget spent (about 97%). ak create splits a budget into shares (rooms, traps, wardens, your delver); this level is sized so every share is nearly spent.
Two hunters come for you; four guards hold their rooms. Do the hunters find you across a board this big?
Four traps, one of your own kind: what does your kind's trap do to you?
On the phone: is the board still readable at this size?

scenarios.title: Full budget: tactics
scenarios.shows: eight large rooms with a minefield and a boss retinue, from the whole budget (96% spent)
focus: Eight large rooms with the whole budget spent (about 96%) through placement tactics: a minefield room and a boss with two minions. ak create splits a budget into shares (rooms, traps, wardens, your delver); this level is sized so every share is nearly spent.
The minefield room has a safe line through its traps: can you find it?
The boss keeps its retinue near: do you pull minions off it first, or go for the boss?

scenarios.title: Gather your gear
scenarios.shows: start with two weak pushes and nothing else, break resources and loot wardens until you are equipped
focus: You start with two weak pushes ({A} and {B}, range 1, intensity 1) and nothing else. An affinity resource gives its affinity only once it is broken, and a restoring kind cannot break anything, so the opposed pair makes sure one push can.
The first resource ({C} pull) is within 3 tiles of the start: push it to break it, then take its affinity from what is left (g). It is drawn R until it is empty.
To use what you took: i, then the affinity's number equips it (a turn). You equip at most three; with all three full, the oldest goes back to your pack.
Find the mana well (a permanent mana boost).
Defeat the wardens and take their affinities from their bodies, also drawn R until emptied. An emptied resource shows * for a moment, then is gone.
Are you fully equipped by the time you reach the exit?

scenarios.title: Earthworks
scenarios.shows: earth barriers against attacking wardens, long corridors to block
focus: You are earth: a push and a pull, with mana for barriers. Three wardens are attacking and come for you down the corridors.

Block a corridor: z, a move key to aim, Enter raises a line of barriers as wide as the push's range, for the push's own mana price (r3 ×2: 3 cells for 48 mana). Earth's barriers get twice the durability of other kinds'.
Wall a warden in: raise barriers around it, then pick it off or leave it boxed.
Watch what the wardens do at a barrier: do they break through, go round, or wait? The hunter's kind changes with the seed; a corrode hunter breaks barriers fast.
Is the mana worth it, or is it cheaper to fight?
